eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects high uncertainty in forecast models for São Paulo's highest temperature on May 11, with implied probabilities tightly clustered at 37.5% for 20°C, 37.0% for 18°C, and 36.0% for 21°C, driven by an advancing cold front from the South. INMET's May 4-11 weekly outlook indicates mostly stable weather in the Southeast with low cloudiness and possible weak showers in southern São Paulo, but the front's timing could introduce southerly winds, increased cloud cover, and rain that suppress peak daytime heating below May climatological averages of 22-23°C. Model ensembles diverge on frontal passage speed—earlier arrival favors 18-19°C maxima via cooler air advection, while delays allow 20-21°C—pending tomorrow's updated INMET and CPTEC guidance. Urban heat island effects at official stations like Mirante de Santana add minor variability to observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket, backed by real capital, prices Munich's May 11 high temperature around 17-19°C, with 38.5% implied probability for 19°C or higher reflecting the latest Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) and ECMWF ensemble means favoring mild advection under a developing upper-level ridge over Central Europe. The tight clustering of 16°C (29%), 17°C (29%), and 18°C (28.5%) probabilities arises from model spread in low-level cloudiness and the timing of a weak cold front, which could suppress daytime heating via reduced insolation or enhance it through clearer skies. Mid-May climatology averages 18°C highs, consistent with guidance; expect volatility from May 10's 12Z forecast updates as resolution nears.

Inherent short-range forecast uncertainty persists; monitor IMGW briefings and ECMWF 12z runs on May 10 for potential adjustments as upper-air patterns evolve. Historical May averages hover near 19°C, providing climatological context for trader positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects deep uncertainty in short-range forecasts for Shenzhen's May 11 high temperature at Bao'an International Airport, with equal 41% implied probabilities for 21°C or below versus 31°C or higher amid divergent model outputs—Shenzhen Meteorological Bureau projecting 30°C under partly cloudy conditions, AccuWeather forecasting 27°C with morning clouds transitioning to afternoon sun. Recent heavy rainfall and thunderstorms across Guangdong on May 8-9, causing flight delays and suppressing diurnal heating via thick cloud cover and high humidity (75-95%), have cooled recent highs to 25-28°C, while a fresh easterly airstream brings slightly cooler coastal air but aloft anticyclone subsidence could enable rapid warming if convection clears. Key differentiators include cloud persistence limiting solar insolation versus sea breeze moderation; watch daily updates from local forecasters for resolution shifts.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 11 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Masroor Airbase Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.
